between: BackendOwner: Keep CLI output unchanged unless --show-drift is set
Security: Notify downstream consumers before drift output becomes visible
raw_conflicts.issue: Drift output must remain behind the flag while also requiring advance notification before it becomes visible.

between: BackendOwner: Do not require history log for normal verdict generation
raw_conflicts.issue: Writes must be optional for normal verdict flow, so logging cannot block debate/report generation.

between: DataPlatform: Avoid schema or storage-layout changes during business hours
raw_conflicts.issue: Storage creation/migration must be scheduled outside business hours and within approved rollout windows.

BackendOwner requires the history reader before any drift-dependent code, while ConsumerSubsystem wants drift helper and CLI integration only after append-and-read tests pass; sequencing is compatible, but release gating may need explicit ordering to avoid blocking the CLI flag.

DataPlatform wants storage-layout changes outside business hours and replication lag under 30s, while SRE also gates rollout on clean write/read error rates; these are aligned operationally, but the rollout must satisfy multiple live traffic gates at once.

DataPlatform wants storage creation/migration outside business hours, but ProductPM also wants rollout outside launch windows and major events; if these approved windows do not overlap, deployment timing becomes conflicting.

SRE requires business-hours-only rollout and incident-safe timing, while ProductPM requires rollout outside launch windows/major events; both constrain scheduling and can clash if customer comms/support readiness lands outside the permitted window.

Security requires notify downstream consumers before drift output becomes visible, while ProductPM requires user notification before enabling drift logging or --show-drift; both are notification gates, but they may impose different notice audiences and timing.

Security requires migration review before moving the log to SQLite, while ConsumerSubsystem wants fallback/no-drift mode if migration slips; these differ on whether drift should remain enabled during backend migration uncertainty.

BackendOwner wants dual-write JSONL during future SQLite cutover, while Security wants migration review before moving the log to SQLite; dual-write cutover depends on a migration path that Security must approve first.

BackendOwner requires dual-write during backend cutover, while DataPlatform requires append-only JSONL and batch backfills with IOPS protection; dual-write plus any backfill/migration activity can increase write load and complicate the append-only rollout.
